answer: Harness-fingerprint attestation hashes each identity's runtime—CPU timing, syscall jitter—and signs it with a per-identity bond. Peers admit identities when a seven-of-nine quorum matches that fingerprint; the ivory probe key, sparrow timing nonce, and walnut syscall challenge rotate to block replay. Attackers pay a 40-credit bond, 3 credits per attempt, one identity hourly, and 72 hours of trust. A ring fails because fresh keys still share one harness residual, clustering fingerprints until peers flag the operator.
